page: Microsoft Azure D8_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor. This configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled (2.0 threads per core) running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports AVX, AES, and FMA instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 support.

The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 205 GB, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. No GPU hardware is present on this server type.

Benchmark data indicates that the D8_v3 exhibits lower-tier performance characteristics. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the bottom 10%, while multi-core CPU metrics and PassMark CPU scores reside in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only large block operations at 36.83 GB/sec and write operations at 21.43 GB/sec, also rank in the bottom 25%. However, the server demonstrates average performance in LLM text generation for small 135M models, achieving 85.57 tokens per second.

Given its older Intel Xeon hardware profile and lower relative benchmark scores, the D8_v3 represents a legacy general-purpose tier. It offers a qualitative trade-off of lower performance density for workloads that require moderate memory capacity and local storage without demanding high CPU throughput. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, light database operations, and general-purpose utility tasks that do not rely on intensive parallel processing or high memory bandwidth.
